newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up as banks stage sharp rally.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up as banks stage sharp rally.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended on a strong note on Monday, boosted by solid gains in the banking sector, pared losses in property counters and a rebound in Japanese share prices, brokers said.
The Hang Seng index closed 97.71 points higher at 13,289.21. Turnover was HK$10.76 billion compared with HK$11.33 billion on Friday.

"The orders are mainly focused on banking stocks. The results announcements will be coming soon so I think investors are taking action first ahead of the results," said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities.

HSBC Holdings is due to release its 1996 earnings on March 3. The stock closed at a record HK$169.50, up HK$1.50, after reaching an all-time high of HK$170.50 during the day. Brokers said talk of a covered warrant issue also boosted the stock.
Shares in Hang Seng Bank closed HK$2.25 higher at HK$93.00 and Bank of East Asia finished up HK$1.50 at HK$36.20.

A 4.7-percent rebound in Tokyo's Nikkei 225 share average to 18,118.79 points also provided local stocks with a lift during the afternoon session, brokers said. "Nobody needs a crisis in the region so the rebound in Japan is certainly helpful," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Property stocks pared their losses during the afternoon.

Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said the government seemed less eager to impose tough measures to limit property speculation in the territory after rising concerns last week that curbs could be imposed soon.
"Generally the market is less sceptical about the measures that will be introduced in the property sector," said So.

Cheung Kong ended HK$0.50 higher at HK$71.75 while Henderson Land closed off HK$0.25 at HK$72.00, after falling to HK$71.00, and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.50 to HK$90.75, after reaching a session low of HK$89.50.

"I think that they will probably stabilise for awhile but I think things have got a little bit ridiculous when stocks are doing well because of there is speculation," said Michael Green, analyst at Salomon Brothers.

"There is froth built on top of froth and when that happens it is good to blow a little bit of the froth off and that is probably far better than everything going to dizzy heights and then crashing down in tears later."

Trading in China Travel International shares was suspended on Monday afternoon. Market sources said they expected the company to raise more than HK$1.6 billion through the issue of 455 million new shares.
